transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um... hi. I guess I'm here because... well, people just keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. 

At work, mostly. Like in my artist statements, or client notes... even when I talk in meetings. They say my thoughts are jumping around too much. Going from, like, textures... to budgets... to secret meanings. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When did you first notice that your thoughts were jumping around like this? Was it something that started recently, or has it been happening for a while?

Um... I guess it's been a while. Maybe... a year and two months? Give or take. 

That's... well, that's when I switched jobs. I left community curation and started doing independent installation work full-time. So... yeah. Around then.
Over this past year or so, have you noticed significant changes in your mood—like periods where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or times when you felt very low or depressed?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. 

There are stretches where I just feel... I don't know, really lit up. Like I'm almost unstoppable, and every idea I have is just brilliant. 

But... I can get irritable, too. If a collaborator makes even a small comment about something, I... I can snap at them. In a way that feels a lot bigger than the situation actually is. So... yeah.
When you have those stretches where you feel really lit up and unstoppable—did those periods of high energy start around the same time as the jumping thoughts, or did one come before the other?

Um... I don't know if they started at the exact same time. It's hard to keep track. 

But those... those stretches where I have all that energy, and I'm irritable, and I'm starting all these projects and barely sleeping... I guess that's been going on for maybe... 10 months? Something like that.
When you're in one of those stretches where you feel really lit up and energetic—how long does that usually last before it goes away? Days? Weeks? Months?

Um... it varies, I guess. Sometimes weeks. Sometimes longer. 

If I really think about it... over the last year, those times where I'm just... going constantly, barely sleeping, snapping at people... they've definitely taken up more of the year than the times when I feel normal. It kind of just... goes up and down, but it's mostly been like that.

When you're not in one of those stretches where you feel really lit up and energetic—when you're back to feeling more normal—how would you describe your mood and energy level during those times? Do you feel pretty much like yourself, or is there something different about those periods too?

Um... well, it's not always normal. 

There was... a quieter month, I guess. I was sleeping more, not feeling so... unstoppable. But... I don't know. 

Even then, I... I was still hearing things. Like... comments coming from behind the shelves in the studio. And... I was still seeing warnings in the materials I use. The paints, the clay... they meant things. That lasted for... a few weeks, even when my energy was lower. So... I guess I didn't feel completely like myself.

When you're in those stretches where you feel really lit up, energetic, and barely sleeping—are you also hearing those comments from behind the shelves or seeing those warnings in the materials during those times too?

Yeah, um... yes. 

When I was... working a lot, and not really sleeping... I was still seeing things in the stains on my materials. And... I thought phrases in emails were giving me instructions on what to make. 

And... sometimes I still heard the woman's voice in the studio, too. So, yeah. It was all happening then, too.

You mentioned hearing that woman's voice and seeing warnings in materials even during the quieter month when your energy was lower. During those times when you felt calmer and were sleeping more—did those voices and warnings feel like they were coming from outside of you, or did they feel like your own thoughts?

Um... outside of me. They aren't... they aren't my thoughts. 

Like I said, when I'm alone in the studio... the woman's voice sounds like she's right there. Just quietly commenting from behind the shelves. It feels completely real. 

And... sometimes I even smell things. Like hot metal near a piece I haven't finished yet. But then I go to check... and there's nothing there. So... yeah. Outside.

When you think back to about a year and two months ago when you first switched jobs—did you start hearing that woman's voice or seeing those warnings in the materials right away, or did those experiences come later, after you'd already been noticing your thoughts jumping around and feeling that high energy?

Um... it didn't start right when I switched jobs. 

The... the messages in the materials, and the voice... and the smells... that all started later. I guess... maybe it's been happening for about eleven months now. So... yeah, it was after the other stuff.

When you first started hearing that woman's voice and seeing the warnings in the materials about eleven months ago—at that same time, were you also experiencing those stretches where you felt really lit up, energetic, barely sleeping, and snapping at people? Or did the high energy and the voices start at different times?

Um... different times, I think. 

The... the high energy stuff, where I wasn't sleeping and took on too many projects... that started a bit later. Maybe... maybe about ten months ago? 

So, no... they didn't start at the exact same time.

When those voices and warnings first started about eleven months ago—at that time, before the high energy and barely sleeping began—would you say your mood and energy were pretty much normal, or were you already starting to feel unusually up or energetic then?

Um... I guess my energy was pretty normal then. 

It was... a quieter month. I was sleeping normally, and I didn't feel... unstoppable or anything yet. But... I still kept hearing those comments from behind the shelves. And reading the hidden warnings into my studio materials... that went on for several weeks like that. 

So... yeah. Just normal energy at first.

During that quieter month when you were sleeping normally and had normal energy—but were still hearing the woman's voice and seeing warnings in the materials—did you feel worried or scared about what you were hearing and seeing? Or did it feel more like something you just accepted as real, without much fear?

Um... I don't really know how I felt. 

It was just... happening. I guess I didn't think much about being scared. It was just... there.

When you think back to that quieter month where you were sleeping normally and had normal energy—but were still hearing the woman's voice and seeing the warnings in the materials—were you feeling down or depressed at all during that time, or would you say your mood was neutral and stable?

Um... I don't think I was depressed. 

Like I said before... it was just a quieter month. I was sleeping normally, not feeling all... unstoppable like I did later. My mood was just... fine, I guess. Stable. But... yeah, I was still hearing those comments from behind the shelves. And seeing those warnings in my studio stuff. That lasted for a few weeks while I was just... normal. So no, not depressed.

When you first started hearing that woman's voice and seeing the warnings in the materials about eleven months ago—before the high energy started—were you also noticing your thoughts jumping around a lot at that same time, or did the racing thoughts start later too?

Um... no, that started later. 

During that first month, my thoughts were... normal. But later, when the energy picked up... that's when my head got crowded. It's like... my thoughts move so fast. Images, titles for pieces, grant language, colors... even conversations. They just... stack on top of each other. I can't even finish one idea before the next one hits. 

But... yeah, that wasn't happening at the very beginning. Just later.

During that first quieter month when you were sleeping normally and had normal energy—and you were hearing the woman's voice and seeing the warnings—did you notice any changes in how you were thinking about yourself or the world around you? Like, did you feel like something was different about reality, or like things had special meanings for you?

Um... I guess things did feel a little different. 

Like... those warnings I mentioned. It wasn't just seeing things. It was... I just knew they were for me. Like, if I saw a certain stain on a canvas, or a specific seam in some fabric... or even just phrases in emails from galleries. I felt like they were instructions. Or warnings about my work. 

And... it's hard to explain, but even if someone else looked at it and said it was just a regular stain or a normal email... I couldn't really let it go. It just felt too specific to me. So... yeah, I guess things had special meanings.

Between the time you first heard that woman's voice and started seeing the warnings—and then about ten months ago when the high energy and racing thoughts started—was there a clear gap of time, like several weeks or more, where you were hearing and seeing those things but hadn't yet started feeling that really lit up, energetic, barely-sleeping feeling?

Um... yes. Like I said... there was that first month. 

I was sleeping fine then. I wasn't... I didn't have all that energy yet. But I was still hearing her... behind the shelves. And seeing the warnings in my supplies. That went on for a few weeks... before everything else started.

Looking back at that first quieter month when you were hearing the woman's voice and seeing the warnings in your materials—before the high energy started—did you feel like your mood was lower or depressed at all, or would you describe it as completely normal and flat?
Um... no, not depressed. I wasn't really sad or anything. I guess my mood was just... normal. Like you said, flat. I was just trying to figure out what the warnings meant. But my mood was fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a clear psychotic disorder with prominent auditory hallucinations (woman's voice behind shelves), visual hallucinations (warnings in materials, stains), olfactory hallucinations (smell of hot metal), and delusions of reference (believing materials and emails contain special messages/instructions meant for her). Critically, psychotic symptoms preceded and persisted independently of mood episodes. The initial presentation ~11 months ago involved psychotic symptoms during a period of normal mood and normal sleep, establishing that psychosis is not solely mood-dependent. While subsequent high-energy episodes with irritability, decreased need for sleep, and racing thoughts occurred (~10 months ago), the psychotic symptoms continued across mood states and predated the energetic episodes. This longitudinal pattern—with primary psychotic symptoms and secondary mood features—is most consistent with F20.0 (Paranoid Schizophrenia) rather than a primary bipolar or schizoaffective disorder.
